text:
ops-bot: ALERT: increase in 504s from canary pool (service: inference-api) — anomaly detected at 2024-11-15T03:21:18Z. Pager sent to oncall-desk and sre-lee.

oncall-desk: acked. looking now, pulling logs.

sre-lee: I see spike in db connection timeouts right after the migration job finished for schema v2. Canary traffic ~5% saw errors, global 0.3% but trending up.

pri: tagging cs-jordan — any customer reports?

cs-jordan: saw 2 customer tickets (enterprise tenants) reporting failed generations. raising to priority.

alex.m: if DB migration is the culprit we should isolate canary traffic ASAP. Suggest flip canary feature flag to route to stable model variant.

oncall-desk: attempting quick mitigation: flipping flag.

oncall-desk: /ff-toggle inference-canary false  -- confirmed command queued (deploy-bot).

deploy-bot: Feature flag infer-canary set to OFF for canary cohort by oncall-desk at 03:25:12Z.

sre-lee: monitoring metrics. initial reduction in 504 slope within 30s. still seeing some lingering 504s from long-running KVs.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20241115-001. Pager duty: oncall-desk -> sre-lee.

pri: good call. next step: do we want to fully rollback the migration or do a targeted DB fix?

sre-lee: quick assessment: migration added an index rebuild which caused connection queueing on a small shard. We can revert migration in prod but that is risky. Prefer to reroute traffic off the affected shards and restart connection pool on worker nodes first.

alex.m: agreed. plan: 1) route canary -> stable (done), 2) restart worker pool that opened long DB connections, 3) flush KV cache for affected shards, 4) if errors persist, schedule migration revert.

oncall-desk: executing step 2: kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-worker -n prod-canary-group.

deploy-bot: kubectl rollout restart started for inference-worker on nodes: i-03a, i-07b, i-12c.

sre-lee: restarting pools now. watching connections.

sre-lee: connection queue depth down from 480 to 10 over 60s. 504s dropped to baseline.

cs-jordan: customers on tickets confirm reduced failures. passing to support to close once stable for 10m.

pri: logging steps for post-incident: need a faster kill-switch in runbook to remove canary entirely from routing, and add migration throttling.

alex.m: also add a smoke test that runs post-migration against a non-critical shard to detect long queries.

oncall-desk: smoke tests: run curl -s -D - -o /dev/null 'https://api.redwood.ai/generate?model=stable' repeated 10 times. All 10 returned 200 within SLO.

ops-bot: Note: automated rollback did NOT trigger because healthcheck threshold for migration was set to 0.7; canaries hit 0.85. We'll update thresholds after postmortem.

sre-lee: assigning follow-up owner: pri will lead the investigation and remediation tasks. pri: can you create a retro and action items?

pri: will do. immediate actions: update runbook, add shard-level migration throttling, add canary kill-switch doc. ETA for tasks: 3 days for runbook changes, 2 weeks for auto-throttle.

cs-jordan: I'll send a customer status note to the impacted tenants: short summary + mitigation steps + points of contact.

alex.m: setting incident status -> mitigated. leaving thread open for retro notes.

oncall-desk: closing pager but keeping postmortem workstream open.

sre-lee: last check: traffic and error rates stable for 12 minutes. marking as resolved in monitoring dashboard.

ops-bot: INC-20241115-001 status: mitigated -> assigned to pri for follow-up. Incident created at 1717245678, resolved at 1717246128.

pri: thanks everyone. I'll post the retro in #postmortems and link this thread.
